review.initial:
Actual GPT-6.1; read-only source/raw review, no independent execution.

**One concrete descriptor-ownership blocker exists in `_refresh`.**

After creating `new`, the code calls `old.close()` before transferring ownership into `state`. If closing `old` raises, `new` is neither stored nor closed. The outer `finally` then closes `state["live"]`—still `old`—again. Because `_Capture.close()` stops on the first close error, this can leak the new capture and retry already-closed old descriptors.

Repair the handoff so every acquired capture has an explicit cleanup owner through close failure. Preserve the primary failure and independently attempt required cleanup; do not simply swallow close errors. Add fault controls for old-close failure before and after partial closure, checking new-capture cleanup and avoiding duplicate-close claims.

The directory extension otherwise appears appropriately scoped: default remains off; changed ancestors require stable identity plus complete child scans and file-generation joins. The tests meaningfully cover unrelated members, missing scan closure, default refusal, known writes followed by refusal and exact retry. They do not establish durable intent, rollback or protected permission.
